newsitem.title: BELGIUM: China seeks advice on deregulation.
newsitem.headline: China seeks advice on deregulation.

text.p: China, stressing the handover of Hong Kong would not alter its status as one of the world's great financial centres, sought advice on Thursday over how to liberalise its financial services sector, officials said.

Sir Leon Brittan, EU Commissioner responsible for relations with China, urged Beijing's State Council Secretary-General Zou Zheng to move ahead with degulation as quickly as possible assuring them it would not lead to collapse of major banks.
"Sir Leon tried to encourage the Chinese to move ahead and assured them deregulation and banking security could go hand in hand," said a Commission spokesman.
Earlier, Lu Ping, China's man responsible for dealing with Hong Kong, told Brittan the British colony's return to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 would not damage its economic well-being in any way.
"He said China would respect all its international undertakings and the political and commercial autonomy of Hong Kong," the spokesman added.
Lu also assured Brittan that other Chinese provinces would be made fully aware of Hong Kong's status and how to deal with it accordingly.
On Wednesday, the Commission said it would monitor the human rights situation in Hong Kong closely after the handover while the European Parliament said it intended to send a fact-finding mission.
Sketching out the new EU policy towards Hong Kong, Brittan said direct economic ties would be put on a permanent footing.
"1997 must mark another step forward in the relationship," he said.
A survey of EU businesses active in China -- released by the Commission on Thursday -- meanwhile showed the remaining obstacles to trade and investment had yet to be removed.
The businesses said a lack of transparency in rules and laws remained the number one problem.
